name: Shealtiel
overview: Shealtiel is a male biblical figure noted primarily for his place in the lineage of the Messiah, as recorded in Luke 3:27. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his role as an ancestor of Christ highlights his importance in the divine genealogy. There are no additional notes that expand on his personal history or attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Shealtiel means 'I have asked [him] of God [El]; possibly God [El] is a shield, God [El] is a victor.' This reveals a name rooted in faith and divine protection, reflecting a trust in God's power and provision as recorded in Luke 3:27.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shealtiel as the father of Neri and, by inference, the father of Zerubbabel, according to Luke 3:27. These relationships place him within a significant ancestral line leading to the Messiah.
scriptureSignificance: Shealtiel's primary significance lies in his position within the Messianic genealogy, linking the Old Testament promises to their fulfillment in Christ. His mention in Luke 3:27 situates him as a key ancestral figure, demonstrating God's providential preservation of the line through which Jesus was born. This underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant and the historical reality of Christ's human ancestry.
